newsitem.title: FRANCE: French analysts say BIS price low.
newsitem.headline: French analysts say BIS price low.

text.p: French financial analysts said that the 490 franc per share price Dutch Vendex International is paying for BIS is low.
Most of the analysts asked said they saw the "fair value" at around 650 francs and there are also some who put the price above 700 francs.

"The debts are low (50 million franc) and the profit margins are improving," an analyst said, adding that after a 1996 profit downturn, due partly to the sale of all assets in 100-percent owned bank Caisse Fonciere de Credit (CFC), the figure should increase in 1997.
Last week, when speculation about a takeover of BIS surfaced, one analyst said an offer would likely be in the range of 700-800 francs per share.
Another had expected the share price to rise to 700 francs on takeover speculation alone without any buyer emerging.
Brokers said that while some investors were likely to sell at 490 when share trading in BIS is set to resume, others are likely to wait and see whether a better price is possible.
BIS was suspended at 533 francs before the market opened on Monday December 30 after chairman and founder Laurent Negro had died that weekend.
